re_line: RBA hikes to 4.85pc, 18-year high · Fiji military rejects coup immunity · NZ poll dead heat four days out · Chinese embassy disputes PNG wharf shell · Solomons moves on anti-defection law
morning_memo: The Reserve Bank raised its cash rate to 4.85 percent, a fifth increase this year and an 18-year high, with Jim Chalmers flagging budget cuts in response.

Fiji's military commander told a parliamentary committee the Republic of Fiji Military Forces opposes immunity for past coup-makers, as Sitiveni Rabuka delays the Constitution (Amendment) Bill's final reading.
New Zealand's National and Labour parties are level in a Reuters-reported poll four days before Saturday's general election.

top_stories.headline: RBA lifts cash rate to 4.85 percent, an 18-year high
top_stories.body: The Reserve Bank raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to *4.85 percent*, the fifth rise this year and the highest level in eighteen years, with board members splitting six to three in favour. The bank said inflation expectations had become entrenched, that inflation would stay above 3 percent for the coming year, and that it would not return to the target band until late 2027. Governor **Michele Bullock** said the economy was not in recession but conceded it "sure feels like one". Treasurer **Jim Chalmers** flagged budget cuts to help bring inflation down.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH: "Chalmers flags budget cuts to fight inflation as interest rates hit 4.85 per cent" · also WSJ: "Australia Central Bank Raises Interest Rates to Highest Level in 18 Years"

top_stories.headline: Fiji military commander opposes coup immunity as constitution bill stalls
top_stories.body: The Republic of Fiji Military Forces told a special parliamentary committee it opposes new immunity provisions for coup-makers in the government's Constitution (Amendment) Bill. Commander **Kalouniwai** said the RFMF did not appear with "clean hands" after the overthrows of 1987, 2000, and 2006, and described an "architecture of rebellion" resting on secrecy, governance through fear, misplaced loyalty, and constitutional immunity. Prime Minister **Sitiveni Rabuka**, who led the 1987 coup, told the committee the country relies on the military during "disruptions", and has delayed the bill's final reading.
top_stories.src_line: per RNZ Pacific: "Fiji military chief urges accountability to the people amid coup immunity debate" · also ABC Pacific Beat: "Fiji PM delays final reading of Constitution Amendment Bill"

top_stories.headline: Chinese embassy disputes PNG police finding on Port Moresby wharf object
top_stories.body: A Papua New Guinea police report, drawing on analysis from an X-ray machine donated by Australia, identifies a shell-shaped object found at a Port Moresby wharf as an undetonated artillery projectile. The Chinese embassy has suggested the item is a wine bottle. The finding follows the investigation into a suspected explosives shipment at the same wharf, last recorded in this brief on October 30.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News (Marian Faa): "Chinese embassy suggests military-grade explosive is actually a wine bottle"

top_stories.headline: Albanese warns Commonwealth leaders on democracy, defends Caribbean trip
top_stories.body: **Anthony Albanese** told the Commonwealth summit in Antigua that threats to democracy are growing, citing the alleged attack on independent MP **Helen Haines**, who had both legs amputated. He is due to meet UK counterpart **Andy Burnham** on rules for British backpackers on working holiday visas. With the Coalition arguing he should not be abroad during the rate decision, Albanese said the government was working "each and every day" to lift living standards, and told reporters "His Majesty invited me".
top_stories.src_line: per SMH: "Albanese warns world leaders of growing threat to democracy after Haines attack" · also The Australian: "PM, King on Forrest climate ship jaunt at CHOGM"

overnight_items.headline: High Court hears constitutional challenge to under-16 social media ban
overnight_items.body_text: Reddit and an Australian digital advocacy group argued in the High Court that the law barring children under sixteen from popular platforms infringes constitutional rights, including freedom of political communication. The hearing is the first substantive legal test of the restriction, which Australia enacted ahead of comparable jurisdictions and which regulators elsewhere have watched closely.

overnight_items.headline: Russian ambassador's wife joins Canberra club, prompting walkout
overnight_items.body_text: Politico's Canberra Playbook reports that the Russian ambassador's wife has joined a Canberra club, prompting other members to walk out. The episode follows Australia's objection to Sergei Lavrov's presence at the G20 ministerial, carried in this brief on October 31, when ministers skipped the family photo.

overnight_items.headline: Two Australians confirmed dead in Spanish high-speed rail disaster
overnight_items.body_text: Spanish authorities have identified two Australians among the 69 people killed when two high-speed trains collided around 130 kilometres south of Madrid, with 500 passengers aboard. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade is providing consular assistance to the families. DFAT said on October 31 it was working to confirm the pair's welfare.

overnight_items.headline: Exporters eye China's interior provinces as beef tariffs bite
overnight_items.body_text: With beef tariffs cutting into returns, Australian exporters and trade officials are looking to China's fast-growing interior provinces for the next round of market gains, The Australian reports. The shift would spread Australian agricultural exposure beyond the coastal cities that have absorbed most trade since the resumption of normal commerce.

overnight_items.headline: Reserve Bank of New Zealand registers Revolut as 27th bank
overnight_items.body_text: New Zealand's central bank has registered the European fintech Revolut as the country's 27th registered bank, Reuters reports. Registration allows it to take deposits in a retail market long dominated by four Australian-owned institutions, days before the general election at which banking competition has featured.

aukus_watch.headline: Calls to renegotiate the AUKUS submarine pact as drone warfare surges
aukus_watch.body_text: The Australian carries the argument that the spread of uncrewed systems has eroded the case for the AUKUS submarine program as structured, and that Canberra should seek to renegotiate. The piece follows this brief's October 30 item on Ghost Shark disclosure and the unresolved readiness question around autonomous undersea platforms.

aukus_watch.headline: Islands Business picks up Australia's defence base spending
aukus_watch.body_text: Islands Business reports that Australia's spending on submarines, fighting vehicles, drones, and jets attracts attention while the billions going into defence bases draws far less. The item follows the Lowy Institute analysis of the $30 billion base build-out carried here on October 29.

pacific_wire.headline: Solomon Islands moves to curb defections with constitutional reform package
pacific_wire.body_text: Prime Minister **Matthew Wale**'s GREAT coalition is advancing a constitutional reform package built on six pillars, including anti-defection measures and limits on the use of motions of no confidence. The government cited unstable coalitions, recurring no-confidence motions, and short parliamentary terms. Wale is recovering in an Australian hospital after leaving Honiara last week for emergency treatment for an undisclosed condition.

pacific_wire.headline: New Zealand opens second Tongan detector dog facility in Vava'u
pacific_wire.body_text: Customs Minister **Casey Costello** opened a locally built detector dog facility in Vava'u, Tonga's second, constructed with help from New Zealand Customs and Police. "We've recognised with organised crime that the Pacific is effectively our collective border," she said, citing the interception of *more than 14 tonnes* of cocaine in the Pacific earlier this year, bound for Australia and New Zealand.

pacific_wire.headline: World Bank releases $11 million for Marshall Islands El Nino and dengue response
pacific_wire.body_text: The World Bank Group has released *$11 million* to Majuro to support the Marshall Islands' response to El Nino impacts, including a dengue outbreak straining public health services. The drought conditions driving the package are the same ones Fiji's agriculture minister warned on November 1 could extend into mid-2027.

pacific_wire.headline: Weapons in circulation raise questions over PNG's 2027 election security
pacific_wire.body_text: Islands Business examines how the large number of weapons in community hands could shape Papua New Guinea's national election, due early in 2027. Election-related violence in the Highlands has repeatedly drawn in police and defence force deployments, with Australian assistance to PNG's electoral and security agencies a recurring feature of past polls.

pacific_wire.headline: Tuvalu parliament replaces century-old public health law
pacific_wire.body_text: Tuvalu's parliament has passed a new Public Health Act, replacing legislation more than a century old and strengthening the state's power to prevent and manage disease outbreaks. The measure lands as Pacific health systems contend with dengue and El Nino-driven water stress across the region.

pacific_wire.headline: Guam votes for governor after a low-key campaign
pacific_wire.body_text: Guam voters went to the polls for a general election headlined by the gubernatorial contest between the Democratic ticket of **Therese Terlaje** and **Sabina Perez** and the Republican ticket of **Tony Ada** and **Edward J. Calvo**. Former attorney general **Alicia Limtiaco**, a Democrat, is challenging Republican incumbent **James Moylan**.

pacific_wire.headline: Pacific states secure protected-areas breakthrough at CBD COP17
pacific_wire.body_text: Pacific Island countries have won proposed recognition of indigenous and traditionally governed areas in biodiversity negotiations at CBD COP17, Islands Business reports. Recognition of customary tenure within protected-area targets has been a standing Pacific negotiating objective in multilateral environmental fora.

pacific_wire.headline: Indonesian bushfire smoke blankets Port Moresby for weeks
pacific_wire.body_text: National Weather Service assistant director **Kasis Inape** said satellite monitoring shows *between 60 and 80 percent* of smoke from Indonesian bushfires is drifting into Papua New Guinea. "There's a lot of carbon monoxide and dangerous gasses which are harmful to health," he said. El Nino is delaying the wet season, raising the prospect the haze persists.

new_zealand.headline: National and Labour level in poll days before New Zealand's election
new_zealand.body_text: A new poll puts National and Labour in a dead heat four days before Saturday's general election, Reuters reports. The result leaves government formation to the minor parties, with advance voting having opened on October 26 and running strongly.

new_zealand.headline: Second Pacific-led medical centre opens in the Wellington region
new_zealand.body_text: The Epuni Medical Centre, owned by Pacific Health Service Hutt Valley, opened on Monday as only the second Pacific-owned and led general practice in the Wellington region, after Porirua. Board chairperson **Au Liko** described it as the fruition of a 27-year effort begun by three Pasifika nurses and chief executive **Nanae Muau**.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Chinese-built Santa Cruz airport handed over in Temotu Province
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: The upgraded Santa Cruz Airport runway and terminal in Temotu Province was handed over last Friday. ABC's Wantok programme reports the project was funded by the World Bank, built by China Harbour Engineering Company, and supervised by Egis, and is the largest project built in Temotu to date. Premier **Stanley Tehiahua** said the airport would support economic development and emergency services in a province far from Honiara.

canberra_politics.headline: First lobbyist sponsorship data shows MPs granting resources and gambling access
canberra_politics.body_text: Labor and Coalition members are sponsoring permanent Parliament House access passes for the country's biggest resources companies and the lobby group representing online gambling giants, according to the first release under updated disclosure rules. The data was thin, with a backlog of *more than 1,000 applications* still unprocessed. The ABC reported the shadow health minister is sponsoring access for Responsible Wagering Australia boss Kai Cantwell, her former chief of staff.

canberra_politics.headline: The Australian reports a $170 billion gap in Labor's forward spending
canberra_politics.body_text: The Australian reports a *$170 billion* hole in the government's forward spending commitments, published hours before the Reserve Bank's fifth rate rise of the year. The paper's editorial ties the figure to questions about the Treasurer's handling of fiscal policy as the bank points to entrenched inflation expectations.

canberra_politics.headline: Labor ministers manage expectations as economic narrative frays
canberra_politics.body_text: **Patricia Karvelas** and **Raf Epstein** report that Labor figures as well as voters are asking "where is the vision, where is the hope" as ministers pre-managed expectations ahead of the rate decision. Victoria is about to enter caretaker mode with its election campaign under way.

canberra_politics.headline: Hanson condemns alleged bat attack on One Nation volunteer in Victoria
canberra_politics.body_text: **Pauline Hanson** called an alleged attack with a bat on a One Nation volunteer in Victoria "so wrong". The incident lands in the same week the Prime Minister used the Commonwealth summit to warn about violence against elected representatives following the alleged attack on Helen Haines.

business_economy.headline: Sharesies among eight Australian brokerages in Anthropic's retail offer
business_economy.body_text: New Zealand-founded platform Sharesies is one of eight Australian brokerages able to participate in Anthropic's proposed Nasdaq listing. Anthropic said the retail component would extend to Australia, Canada, Japan, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and nine European Economic Area states.

business_economy.headline: Bloomberg opinion holds up New Zealand as a cautionary tale for the Fed
business_economy.body_text: Bloomberg argues the Federal Reserve under Warsh should study New Zealand's monetary policy experience before changing course. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand pioneered inflation targeting, and its record is routinely cited in debates over central bank mandates.

primary_documents.headline: Pacific ministers reaffirm unity ahead of Palau meeting
primary_documents.body_text: Pacific ministers have reaffirmed regional unity ahead of a meeting in Palau, FBC News reports from the ministerial readout. Palau's President Surangel Whipps Jr took the Forum chair from Solomon Islands Prime Minister Jeremiah Manele at the 55th Leaders Meeting in Koror.

calendar_watch.event: United States midterm elections, all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Control of Congress bears on authorisation and appropriation for AUKUS-related submarine industrial base measures.
A dead-heat poll four days out leaves defence and foreign policy continuity dependent on minor-party coalition arithmetic.

calendar_watch.event: Victoria enters caretaker mode ahead of its state election
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Caretaker conventions suspend new state commitments, including on Treaty and major procurement, during the campaign.
Weapons in community circulation raise the security burden on PNG agencies and on Australian electoral and policing assistance.

key_stat.label: World Bank release for Marshall Islands El Nino response
key_stat.context: The package funds the response to drought impacts and a dengue outbreak as El Nino conditions persist across the north Pacific.

also_today.headline: The power broker in New Zealand's election has no foreign policy
also_today.body_text: The Interpreter argues the party likely to hold the balance of power after Saturday's vote has no articulated foreign policy, leaving external settings to be negotiated after the fact.

also_today.headline: Lowy: Chinese assertiveness and US uncertainty push India and Australia closer on defence
also_today.body_text: The Lowy Institute argues the combination of Chinese assertiveness and uncertainty about United States commitments is accelerating defence cooperation between New Delhi and Canberra.

also_today.headline: Forward defence in depth: how to preserve Australia's strategy of denial
also_today.body_text: ASPI argues the strategy of denial set out in the National Defence Strategy requires the ADF to reduce an adversary's confidence that force or coercion can achieve its objectives, and that current force structure falls short.

also_today.headline: Australia's defence investment must build the industry to sustain a fight
also_today.body_text: ASPI argues billions committed to capability, infrastructure, and preparedness are not yet producing the scalable industrial base, particularly in drones and Northern Territory sustainment, needed to sustain a conflict.

also_today.headline: Australia barely owns a ship but moves the world's heaviest cargo and carbon
also_today.body_text: The Interpreter argues Australia's position as a bulk exporter gives Canberra leverage over shipping decarbonisation rules despite owning almost no vessels.

also_today.headline: Australia's small business strategy must make employing and growing easier
also_today.body_text: ASPI argues economic resilience, domestic capability, and secure supply chains depend on a growing small-business sector that current national policy settings overlook.

also_today.headline: WA minister details misogynistic abuse that has not abated since Haines attack
also_today.body_text: Western Australian Women's Interests Minister **Simone McGurk**, first elected in 2013, said she had "never seen such hatred and vitriol" in politics and that abuse of her and her staff had not diminished since the alleged attack on Helen Haines.

also_today.headline: Pacific governments struggle to regulate the lucrative sea cucumber trade
also_today.body_text: ABC Pacific reports that governments across the region are failing to manage a high-value sea cucumber export trade, with enforcement and licensing capacity lagging demand from Asian markets.
